paragraphs: Federated learning lets clients train a shared model while keeping their raw data local. This paper studies a setting where clients use different model architectures and participate with different probabilities. Those differences create a fairness problem: improving overall accuracy does not necessarily produce balanced performance across clients that contribute at unequal rates.

The proposed PHP-FL method addresses both sources of variation. Its DEAL module places small auxiliary models on clients to support knowledge alignment and local ensemble learning. This allows different client models to collaborate without requiring a public dataset. Its ISPU module selectively updates important local parameters according to training progress, aiming to reduce update conflicts associated with unequal participation.

The authors implement PHP-FL on a lightweight federated learning platform and evaluate heterogeneous clients under three participation patterns. They report state-of-the-art accuracy and performance fairness across the tested settings. The contribution is a method that explicitly treats participation differences and architectural differences together, making fairness part of the learning design rather than relying on uniform participation.
neurips-2025-a-fair-federated-learning-m.tldr: PHP-FL improves reported accuracy and fairness when federated clients have different models and unequal chances of participating.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to explore a network when inspecting a node reveals an unknown label and earns a reward determined by that label. Labels follow a joint distribution with a graph-based Markov structure. Exploration must stay on the frontier: each new node must neighbor one already selected. This captures constraints found in contact tracing and robotic exploration.

The objective is to choose nodes adaptively to maximize expected accumulated rewards, with later rewards discounted. The authors develop a policy based on Gittins indices that can operate on general graphs. They prove optimality when the graph is a forest, meaning it contains no cycles. The implementation has quadratic dependence on node count in its running time, alongside dependence on the number of possible labels.

Experiments on synthetic and real networks show improvements over natural baselines, including settings with cycles, limited budgets, or no discounting. In HIV testing simulations on real sexual interaction networks, the policy finds nearly all positive cases after testing half the population. That simulation result extends the empirical evidence beyond the forest setting covered by the optimality guarantee.
neurips-2025-adaptive-frontier-explorati.tldr: A frontier-constrained graph exploration policy is provably optimal on forests and performs strongly in network-based disease testing simulations.

paragraphs: Probabilistic forecasting aims to describe possible future values and their uncertainty. This paper adapts Generative Flow Networks to construct time-series forecasts step by step. These networks learn to sample completed objects in proportion to a reward signal. Applying that idea to continuous measurements requires bridging the gap between continuous values and discrete generation actions.

Temporal GFNs represent time-series segments as states and generate future values by choosing quantized actions. An adaptive training curriculum changes the number of available bins using reward improvement and policy entropy. This balances finer numerical resolution against exploration. A straight-through estimator supplies discrete samples for building trajectories while allowing continuous approximations to carry gradients during training.

The training objective combines trajectory balance, which encourages consistent flows through the generation process, with entropy regularization. The authors also derive theoretical bounds on the effect of quantization error and on the adaptive factor's range. The contribution is a principled construction for bringing structured, reward-based generation into continuous forecasting, with explicit treatment of discretization and trainability.
neurips-2025-adaptive-quantization-in-ge.tldr: Temporal GFNs use adaptive discretization and gradient-compatible sampling to construct probabilistic forecasts of continuous time series.

paragraphs: Machine-generated text detectors are usually trained as though their labels provide an exact standard. This paper argues that ambiguity at the boundary between human and machine-generated text makes that assumption unreliable. It proposes improving supervision by drawing on an easier detection task, rather than treating every supplied label as equally dependable evidence.

The framework uses a supervisor that examines longer texts, even if that supervisor has weaker capabilities than the target detector. The authors theoretically argue that longer passages reduce the influence of inexact labels. They also structurally incorporate the detector into the supervisor and model the supervisor's performance as a lower bound for the detector. Under this construction, optimizing the supervisor indirectly improves the detector.

Experiments cover changes in the generating language model, changes in text domain, mixed text, and paraphrase attacks. The authors report significant detection effectiveness across these settings. The central idea is that a more manageable task can supply useful supervision for a harder one, with the framework seeking to approximate the underlying labels despite ambiguity in the available training signal.
neurips-2025-advancing-machine-generated.tldr: An easy-to-hard training framework uses longer-text detection to improve supervision when machine-generated text labels are ambiguous.

paragraphs: This paper studies learning from a continuously changing stream when the learner can query it and update only at selected moments. The data may be noisy or non-stationary. The central question is how much performance is lost when interaction is limited, rather than assuming that the learner observes a new labeled example at every discrete step.

For streams that do not react to the learner, the authors give a reduction to classical online learning. If a discrete-time method has regret R(S) after S interactions, their construction yields regret T times R(S) divided by S over a time horizon T. For streams that respond to learner actions, they combine dynamic query timing with importance weighting to estimate losses without bias.

For hypothesis classes with finite Littlestone dimension, the paper establishes matching regret bounds up to logarithmic factors in both settings. Regret scales with the time horizon and with the square root of class complexity divided by query budget. This quantifies how additional observations can improve learning and how a more complex hypothesis class increases the difficulty of sparse interaction.
neurips-2025-agnostic-continuous-time-on.tldr: The paper characterizes how query budgets and hypothesis complexity govern regret when learning from continuous-time streams.

paragraphs: Decoding text from fMRI requires relating a long sequence of brain measurements to language. The paper identifies a problem with processing the entire sequence at once: memory demands and semantic drift can degrade decoding as inputs grow longer. Its approach uses incremental processing inspired by segmented language comprehension to keep the decoding process coherent.

The framework divides the fMRI time series into consecutive segments matched to a language comprehension length. It decodes each segment, summarizes its meaning through a wrap-up mechanism, and uses that summary as prior knowledge for later segments. A second component improves representation learning: attention to important text tokens guides which fMRI time points are masked in a masked autoencoder.

The masking task directs learning toward brain activity associated with semantically salient moments, while the wrap-up process carries meaning across segment boundaries. On two datasets, the authors report significant improvements over state-of-the-art approaches, with larger gains at longer decoding lengths. These findings support the combined use of selective representation learning and sequential semantic summarization for the evaluated fMRI-to-text tasks.
neurips-2025-brain-inspired-fmri-to-text.tldr: Incremental decoding, semantic summaries, and text-guided masking improve fMRI-to-text results, especially for longer sequences.

paragraphs: Choosing a neural architecture for structured data remains difficult because images, point clouds, graphs, and meshes organize information differently. This paper introduces copresheaf topological neural networks, or CTNNs, as a common mathematical framework for designing models across these settings. The aim is to give architectural choices a shared foundation while retaining sensitivity to the structure of the data.

The framework uses copresheaves, a concept from algebraic topology, to express a broad range of neural architectures. The authors present this formulation as constructive: it defines a design space from which models can be derived. They connect that space to challenges including long-range dependencies, representations becoming overly similar, connections between unlike graph nodes, and data living on non-Euclidean domains.

On structured-data benchmarks, the authors report consistent improvements over conventional baselines, particularly when tasks require hierarchical or localized sensitivity. Those results support the practical value of the proposed mathematical formulation in the tested settings. The broader contribution is a multi-scale approach to architecture design that brings several kinds of structured-data learning into one framework.
neurips-2025-copresheaf-topological-neur.tldr: CTNNs use copresheaves to unify structured-data neural architecture design and report gains on tasks requiring local or hierarchical sensitivity.

paragraphs: Low-light video enhancement can combine RGB images with event-camera data, but the paper identifies two weaknesses in existing approaches. They are often tuned for steady lighting, and they expect both sensors to remain available. Changing illumination or losing a sensing modality can therefore undermine video quality in the situations where enhancement is needed.

EVDiffuser uses a video diffusion model with RGB and event inputs treated as optional conditions. This conditioning mechanism allows the same pipeline to operate with both modalities or with either one alone. The model is fine-tuned using augmented and integrated datasets. A guidance rescaling mechanism adjusts how strongly each modality contributes according to its sensor-specific characteristics.

The authors also introduce a benchmark covering varying illumination and diverse real-world scenarios. Their experiments report state-of-the-art performance in challenging lighting conditions and across sensor configurations, including event-only and RGB-only inputs. The contribution combines flexible sensing with video diffusion priors, supporting consistent enhancement in the evaluated settings even when the available input modalities change.
neurips-2025-event-guided-consistent-vid.tldr: EVDiffuser adapts video enhancement to changing illumination and optional RGB or event inputs through flexible diffusion conditioning.

paragraphs: Extended light field microscopy can capture volumetric information in a single exposure over a broad field of view. Reconstructing a three-dimensional volume from those measurements requires using both spatial and angular information. This paper addresses two obstacles to learned reconstruction: a lack of standardized evaluation data and difficulty combining efficient representations with the microscope's imaging physics.

The authors introduce the XLFM-Zebrafish dataset and evaluation suite. They also propose Masked View Modeling for Light Fields, a self-supervised task that predicts hidden views to learn relationships across viewing angles. A separate optical rendering consistency loss ties the reconstructed volume to the measurement process by comparing its point-spread-function-based forward projections with the observed data.

These components connect learning from incomplete views with checking whether a predicted volume agrees with the optical formation process. On the XLFM-Zebrafish benchmark, the method improves PSNR by 7.7% over state-of-the-art baselines. The stated result supports the combination of angular representation learning and physical consistency for reconstruction, while the benchmark provides a common setting for evaluating such methods.
neurips-2025-from-pixels-to-views-learni.tldr: A zebrafish microscopy benchmark, masked-view learning, and optical consistency constraints improve learned volumetric reconstruction.

paragraphs: Ride-hailing systems must respond to supply and demand that change across locations and over time. This paper targets a gap between reinforcement learning approaches, which can require substantial interaction data, and decomposed optimization systems, whose manually chosen high-level objectives may overlook routing details. It proposes connecting objective design directly to feedback from operational optimization.

An LLM acts as a meta-optimizer, producing semantic heuristics that guide a lower-level mathematical optimizer. The lower level enforces constraints and executes real-time decisions. A closed-loop evolutionary process driven by harmony search refines the LLM prompts using feedback about feasibility and performance. The framework is training-free, avoiding the large-scale interaction training required by the reinforcement learning approaches discussed.

Experiments use scenarios derived from New York and Chicago taxi datasets. The authors report an average improvement of 16% over state-of-the-art baselines. The result supports their division of responsibilities: language-based heuristics adapt high-level objectives, while mathematical optimization handles operational execution. Feedback between those levels is the mechanism intended to keep strategic guidance connected to routing dynamics.
neurips-2025-hierarchical-optimization-v.tldr: A training-free framework evolves LLM-generated objectives using optimizer feedback and reports a 16% average improvement in taxi-derived scenarios.

paragraphs: Outsourcing model training can expose an institution to backdoors inserted through poisoned training data. This paper studies a semi-honest setting in which providers are assumed to follow prescribed training protocols. Its detection strategy cross-examines models from two independent service providers, looking for inconsistencies that can reveal hidden trigger-dependent behavior across different learning paradigms.

The framework uses central kernel alignment to compare internal features even when models differ in architecture or training paradigm. Those comparisons support the recovery and identification of candidate backdoor triggers. It then analyzes sensitivity to fine-tuning to distinguish backdoor triggers from adversarial perturbations, reducing false positives caused by confusing these two kinds of model vulnerability.

The authors report detection accuracy improvements of 4.4%, 1.7%, and 10.6% over state-of-the-art baselines in supervised, semi-supervised, and autoregressive tasks, respectively. They also report effective backdoor detection in multimodal large language models. The approach's broad applicability comes from combining cross-provider comparisons with a second test of trigger behavior, within the stated outsourced-training setting.
neurips-2025-lie-detector-unified-backdo.tldr: Lie Detector compares independently trained models and tests fine-tuning sensitivity to identify backdoors across several learning paradigms.

paragraphs: Meta-black-box optimization uses learning to automate parts of optimization algorithm design. It has two levels: a higher-level policy learns how to guide lower-level optimization tasks. MetaBox-v2 expands an earlier platform focused on reinforcement learning and single-objective problems, providing a shared environment for a wider range of approaches and evaluation scenarios.

The platform supports reinforcement learning, evolutionary, and gradient-based methods, with reproductions of 23 baselines. Its parallelization schemes reportedly reduce training and testing time by factors of 10 to 40. The benchmark suite contains 18 synthetic or realistic tasks and more than 1,900 instances, spanning single-objective, multi-objective, multi-model, and multi-task settings. Extensible interfaces support analysis, visualization, and connections to external tools.

The authors demonstrate the platform through a systematic comparison of optimization performance, generalization, and learning efficiency. These are complementary questions: a method's effectiveness on a task is only one aspect of how useful its learned optimization behavior may be. The contribution is shared infrastructure for making those comparisons across a broader set of methods and problems.
neurips-2025-metabox-v2-a-unified-benchm.tldr: MetaBox-v2 broadens meta-optimization benchmarking with 23 baselines, diverse tasks, and reported 10–40-fold training and testing speedups.

paragraphs: Electromyographic recordings combine activity from multiple motor units. Decomposition methods try to separate that mixture into individual spike trains, providing a view of the nervous system's motor output. The paper identifies a benchmarking gap: available evaluation resources do not adequately cover the muscles, movements, and noise sources encountered in practice.

MUniverse brings together simulation, datasets, decomposition pipelines, and standardized evaluation. Its simulation interface connects to a state-of-the-art EMG generator. The dataset library includes synthetic recordings, hybrid synthetic-real data with known spikes, and experimental EMG. Internal and external decomposition pipelines provide methods to evaluate, while common tasks, metrics, and baseline results establish a shared comparison process.

The suite is designed to support extension and reproducibility, with datasets distributed using Croissant and BIDS metadata standards. Its main contribution is infrastructure for testing decomposition methods across varied conditions and generating datasets at scale. Known spikes in the supported simulated and hybrid data give evaluation a direct reference, while experimental recordings broaden the kinds of signals represented in the suite.
neurips-2025-muniverse-a-simulation-and-.tldr: MUniverse standardizes simulation, datasets, pipelines, and evaluation for separating motor-unit spike activity from EMG recordings.

paragraphs: Large reasoning models generate intermediate reasoning before producing an answer. This paper shows how that iterative process can become a resource-exhaustion vulnerability. Its Deadlock Attack uses an adversarial embedding to encourage repeated transitions into further reasoning, preventing the model from concluding and pushing generation toward the available token limit.

A central finding is that an embedding-level attack does not transfer straightforwardly into ordinary input tokens. The authors identify a continuous-to-discrete projection gap: naive conversion of the optimized embedding into a token sequence removes its effect. Their approach therefore introduces a backdoor implantation strategy that allows specific trigger tokens to activate the behavior reliably.

Across four reasoning models and three mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the authors report 100% attack success, with models generating up to their maximum token limits. They also report negligible utility loss on benign inputs and persistence against existing overthinking mitigations. These results identify a control-flow vulnerability in the evaluated backdoored systems, where apparently normal task performance coexists with trigger-induced failure to finish reasoning.
neurips-2025-one-token-embedding-is-enou.tldr: An adversarial embedding activated through a backdoor makes tested reasoning models continue thinking until they exhaust their token limits.

paragraphs: Comparisons between visual brain activity and neural networks have produced conflicting conclusions about their similarity. This paper asks a more focused question: do their internal representations support similar decisions on individual images? It introduces decision variable correlation, or DVC, to compare decision strategies rather than measuring broad alignment between representations.

DVC correlates decoded decisions image by image within a classification task. The authors apply it to monkey V4 and IT recordings and to image-classification networks. They find that similarities between models are comparable to similarities between monkeys, while similarities between models and monkeys are consistently lower. DVC also decreases as the evaluated networks' ImageNet-1k performance increases.

Adversarial training increases model-to-model similarity but does not improve model-to-monkey similarity in the task-relevant dimensions measured by DVC. Pre-training on larger datasets likewise does not improve that cross-system similarity. Together, these results suggest that better image classification and stronger agreement among models need not bring their decision-related representations closer to those observed in monkey visual cortex.
neurips-2025-quantifying-task-relevant-s.tldr: Decision variable correlation reveals a gap between model and monkey decision-related representations that stronger image-classification performance does not close.

paragraphs: Learning how partial differential equations map inputs to solutions is difficult when the physical domain can take many shapes. The model must accommodate both geometric variation and the underlying physics. RIGNO addresses this problem with a graph neural network that learns solution operators from data represented as point clouds on arbitrary domains.

Its multi-scale architecture transfers information between input and output point clouds through a downsampled regional mesh. This intermediate representation provides a coarser structure through which the model processes the data. The design also includes components aimed at preserving behavior when spatial or temporal resolution changes, so the learned mapping can be applied beyond the sampling resolutions encountered during training.

The authors evaluate RIGNO on benchmarks containing both time-dependent and steady equations across diverse domains. They report significantly better accuracy than neural operator baselines and robust generalization to unseen resolutions in space and time. These findings support the combination of point-cloud inputs, regional processing, and resolution-aware design for learning PDE solution mappings across the tested geometries and physical problems.
neurips-2025-rigno-a-graph-based-framewo.tldr: RIGNO learns PDE solution operators through point clouds and a regional mesh, with strong accuracy and generalization to unseen resolutions.

paragraphs: Most visual representation systems assign every image the same amount of representational space. This paper instead draws on algorithmic information theory: an informative representation should compress an input while retaining what is needed to predict its content. Images that differ in complexity or familiarity may therefore call for different numbers of tokens.

KARL predicts that token allocation in a single forward pass. It stops when it reaches an approximate measure of Kolmogorov complexity, with token count serving as a proxy for minimum description length. This avoids the test-time search across multiple candidate representations used by other adaptive tokenizers. The authors report performance comparable to recent adaptive methods while retaining one-pass operation.

The paper also investigates what adaptive tokenization reveals about image complexity and interestingness. It reports empirical signals approximating concepts such as sophistication and logical depth, along with alignment to human annotations across structure-versus-noise and familiarity comparisons. These are conceptual and empirical connections to algorithmic information theory; the token counts function as approximations rather than exact shortest-program measurements.
neurips-2025-single-pass-adaptive-image-.tldr: KARL allocates image tokens in one pass, matching recent adaptive tokenizers while using token count as an approximate description-length measure.

paragraphs: A Neural Radiance Field represents an object's geometry and appearance in the parameters of a neural network. Language models can be given those parameters to describe or answer questions about the object. The paper argues that earlier weight-based approaches compress the object into a global representation that does not adequately support detailed spatial understanding.

The proposed weights2space framework learns, without supervision, to turn NeRF weights into a sequence of spatial tokens. A meta-encoder performs this conversion directly from the network parameters. The authors then build Spatial LLaNA around that representation, giving a multimodal language model spatially organized information for understanding object details and relationships.

Evaluation covers NeRF captioning and question answering using existing benchmarks and a new dataset, Spatial ObjaNeRF. The new dataset contains 100 manually curated language annotations for NeRFs, with models and descriptions chosen to challenge spatial reasoning. Spatial LLaNA outperforms existing approaches across the evaluated tasks. The results support preserving spatial structure when converting neural object representations into language-model inputs.
neurips-2025-spatially-aware-weights-tok.tldr: Spatial LLaNA converts NeRF weights into spatial tokens to improve object captioning and question answering about details and relationships.

paragraphs: Sparse perception models use queries to interpret driving scenes without explicitly building dense bird's-eye-view or volumetric representations. This supports efficient computation and inference. The paper introduces SQS, a pre-training method designed to improve the contextual information learned by those sparse queries before they are used for specific three-dimensional perception tasks.

During pre-training, a plug-in module predicts 3D Gaussian representations from the queries. Self-supervised splatting reconstructs images from multiple views and depth maps, encouraging the queries to capture fine-grained scene context. During fine-tuning, interaction mechanisms explicitly connect these pre-trained Gaussian queries with task-specific queries. That connection allows the learned representation to support both occupancy prediction and object detection.

Experiments on autonomous-driving benchmarks report gains across multiple query-based perception tasks. Compared with prior state-of-the-art pre-training approaches, SQS improves occupancy prediction by 1.3 mIoU and 3D detection by 1.0 NDS. The findings support reconstruction-based pre-training as a way to enrich sparse representations, with query interactions providing the link from the shared pre-training task to distinct downstream objectives.
neurips-2025-sqs-enhancing-sparse-percep.tldr: SQS pre-trains sparse scene queries through Gaussian splatting and reconstruction, improving occupancy prediction and 3D object detection.

paragraphs: When training must stop after a fixed number of iterations, the learning-rate schedule affects how much progress fits within that budget. Common schedules often rely on heuristic choices and repeated tuning. This paper proposes the Unified Budget-Aware schedule, or UBA, derived from an optimization framework that explicitly includes the available training budget.

The framework accounts for robustness to changes in the curvature of the optimization landscape. Its resulting schedule is controlled by one parameter, phi, balancing flexibility with simplicity and avoiding per-network numerical optimization. The authors connect phi theoretically to the condition number, prove convergence for different parameter values, and provide selection guidance based on both theory and experiments.

Experiments span vision and language tasks, multiple model architectures and scales, and different iteration budgets. The authors report that UBA consistently outperforms commonly used schedules in these evaluations, including settings involving ResNet and OLMo. The contribution combines an interpretable schedule family with practical parameter guidance, making limited training time an explicit design consideration rather than an afterthought.
neurips-2025-stepsize-anything-a-unified.tldr: UBA derives a single-parameter, budget-aware learning-rate schedule and reports consistent gains across evaluated vision and language training settings.

paragraphs: A robot that learns several basic tasks should ideally be able to combine them into a longer task. That requires representations whose pieces remain useful when placed together in a new sequence. This paper investigates how to learn such representations automatically, addressing the gap between recognizing individual tasks and carrying out compound instructions.

The proposed approach uses a temporal alignment loss to associate representations of current states with representations of future states. This gives representation learning an explicit connection to how a task unfolds over time. The authors show that this association can improve compositional generalization without adding explicit subtask planning or reinforcement learning. The intervention is therefore in how task information is represented and aligned.

Evaluation includes diverse robotic manipulation tasks and simulation, with tasks specified either through language or goal images. The authors report substantial improvements across these settings. The findings indicate that temporally aligned representations can help learned behaviors compose into multi-step tasks, and that the benefit in the reported evaluations is not confined to a single instruction format.
neurips-2025-temporal-representation-ali.tldr: Aligning representations of current and future states improves robots' compositional task generalization without explicit subtask planning or reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: EEG contains activity distributed across multiple channels as well as changes over time. The paper argues that autoregressive models built around straightforward temporal sequences miss important physiological structure and spatial dynamics. THD-BAR changes the organization of the prediction problem so that spatial hierarchy becomes part of what the model learns.

Its Brain Topology Hierarchy establishes an ordering of EEG channels at multiple spatial scales. This turns autoregressive learning into prediction across both scale and time. A topology-hierarchical vector-quantized variational autoencoder converts the data into multi-scale tokens, and an enhanced Brain Autoregressive module uses specialized masking strategies to predict them. Together, these components integrate the hierarchy into both representation construction and prediction.

The authors pre-train on 17 datasets and evaluate on 10 downstream datasets covering five tasks. They report consistent improvements over existing methods. Those results support the value of representing EEG through a spatial hierarchy alongside temporal progression, with the range of downstream evaluations providing evidence for generalization across the tested tasks.
neurips-2025-thd-bar-topology-hierarchic.tldr: THD-BAR organizes EEG prediction across spatial scales and time, improving results across five downstream task types.

paragraphs: This paper studies resource allocation under matroid constraints, a mathematical setting that includes bipartite matching. Agents belong to groups defined by a sensitive attribute. Opportunity fairness requires each group to receive the same proportion of the maximum allocation it could obtain on its own, so fairness is measured relative to each group's feasible opportunity.

The authors quantify the cost of that requirement through the Price of Fairness: the largest unconstrained allocation divided by the largest opportunity-fair allocation. They characterize this ratio using the problem's underlying polymatroid structure. That characterization supports bounds across settings ranging from adversarially chosen problems to random ones, connecting fairness costs to structural properties of the allocation problem.

One main result allows an arbitrary matroid but assumes agents are randomly divided into groups. In that setting, the bound depends on the relative size of the largest group. The authors conclude that, when no group is too dominant under these conditions, opportunity fairness causes no loss in allocation size. This identifies a setting where fairness and the stated social-welfare objective can coexist without a trade-off.
neurips-2025-the-price-of-opportunity-fa.tldr: The paper characterizes opportunity fairness costs and identifies random-group settings where fairness preserves maximum allocation size.

paragraphs: Medical retrieval-augmented generation usually draws on explicit knowledge sources. This paper argues that similar patient cases offer another useful form of evidence, reflecting the role of experience in clinical reasoning. DoctorRAG combines these two sources so that generated responses can draw on both clinical knowledge and relevant patient analogies.

The framework assigns conceptual tags to queries and knowledge sources to improve retrieval precision. A hybrid retrieval mechanism then gathers relevant knowledge and patient information. Its Med-TextGrad module uses textual gradients from multiple agents to refine the output, aiming to keep the response consistent with the retrieved evidence and the patient's query. Retrieval and iterative refinement therefore address different parts of the response process.

Experiments span multiple languages and tasks. The authors report significant improvements over strong RAG baselines, with further gains from iterative refinement and responses described as more accurate, relevant, and comprehensive. The findings support integrating case-based experience with explicit knowledge in the evaluated medical question-answering settings, advancing the paper's goal of more doctor-like reasoning.
neurips-2025-towards-doctor-like-reasoni.tldr: DoctorRAG combines clinical knowledge, similar patient cases, and iterative textual feedback to improve medical retrieval-augmented responses.

paragraphs: Mobile interface agents need to determine whether their actions actually complete a task, and they need enough high-quality examples to improve. UI-Genie addresses these linked problems with a reward model and an iterative data-generation pipeline. The reward model evaluates both individual actions and overall task outcomes while processing the interaction's historical context.

UI-Genie-RM interleaves image and text information. Its training data are produced through rule-based verification, controlled corruption of action trajectories, and hard negative mining. The self-improvement pipeline uses reward-guided exploration and outcome verification in dynamic environments to improve both the agent and reward model. Successive rounds expand the set of complex interface tasks the system can solve.

The authors release UI-Genie-RM-517k and UI-Genie-Agent-16k and report high-quality synthetic trajectory generation without manual annotation. Across three generations of data-model improvement, UI-Genie achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple GUI-agent benchmarks. The contribution ties verification to learning: outcome assessment supports new training data, and that data is used to improve the models participating in subsequent rounds.
neurips-2025-ui-genie-a-self-improving-a.tldr: UI-Genie improves mobile GUI agents through reward-based outcome verification and three rounds of synthetic-data-driven self-improvement.
